title: Harnessing Post-selected von Neumann Measurements to Strengthen Entanglement and Quantum Signatures in Coherent States
authors: Janarbek Yuanbek, Zelalem Abebe Bekele, Zhi-qiang Liu
abstract: We investigate how post-selected von Neumann measurements modify the nonclassical properties of two-mode entangled coherent states (ECSs). From the conditional pointer state, we characterize squeezing, photon statistics, intermode correlations, entanglement, fidelity, and post-selection probability. Anomalous weak values with moderate coupling enhance squeezing, antibunching, sub-Poissonian statistics, intermode correlations, and bipartite entanglement, while fidelity captures the crossover from weak perturbation to strong distinguishability. These results demonstrate post-selection as a tunable approach to engineering ECSs.
summary: This theoretical paper examines how performing post-selected von Neumann measurements alters the quantum characteristics of two-mode entangled coherent states. By analyzing observables like squeezing and photon statistics, the authors demonstrate that this measurement process acts as a tunable mechanism to enhance nonclassicality, confirming post-selection's utility in quantum state engineering.
main_problem: The paper investigates how post-selected von Neumann measurements (PVNMs) modify the nonclassical properties of two-mode entangled coherent states (ECSs). It aims to show that post-selection can be a tunable method for engineering these quantum states.
main_result: Anomalous weak values, particularly under moderate coupling, enhance key nonclassical features such as squeezing, antibunching, sub-Poissonian statistics, and bipartite entanglement in ECSs.
method: The analysis involves calculating the conditional pointer state resulting from PVNMs and characterizing various quantum diagnostics on this state.
model_or_system: The system under study is two-mode entangled coherent states (ECSs), which are non-Gaussian continuous-variable states. The theoretical framework utilizes a measurement interaction Hamiltonian and analyzes the resulting conditional pointer state.
key_observables: Squeezing ($\Delta^2 F_i$), photon statistics (Mandel Q parameter, $g^{(2)}$), intermode correlations, entanglement (Hillery-Zubairy correlation $E$), and fidelity.
important_parameters: Measurement strength parameter $s = g t / \sigma$, and the coupling strength $g$ and time $t$. The analysis covers weak ($s \ll 1$) and strong ($s \gg 1$) coupling regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an ideal von Neumann measurement context where the measurement interaction Hamiltonian dominates the evolution.

paper_structure: The paper systematically builds upon the weak measurement framework, first defining the physical system (ECSs) and the measurement protocol. It then calculates and analyzes multiple nonclassical observables (squeezing, statistics, entanglement) as functions of the measurement strength parameter, culminating in the demonstration of post-selection's engineering capability.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, as it explores how measurement back-action (specifically post-selection) can be used as a precise tool to enhance or engineer nonclassical features in continuous-variable quantum states.
